headline_marked: [[Police officer stabbed]] while attempting to arrest drug dealer in Chattogram
headline: Police officer stabbed while attempting to arrest drug dealer in Chattogram
summary: Sub-Inspector Mobinul Islam was attacked by a gang of miscreants during an operation in the Ambagan area.
details: A police officer was stabbed and another injured while attempting to arrest a listed drug dealer in the Ambagan area of Chattogram city last night.
The injured officer has been identified as Sub-Inspector (SI) Mobinul Islam of Double Mooring Police Station.
The incident took place around 8:00pm on Saturday in the Jharna Para area under Double Mooring Police Station.
Additional Commissioner of Chattogram Metropolitan Police (PR) Aminur Rashid confirmed the incident to The Daily Star.
SI Mobinul Islam was attacked by the suspect and his gang while trying to arrest Alamgir, an accused in drug cases.
The injured officer is currently receiving treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH).
Police have arrested the listed drug dealer Alamgir, and drives are underway to arrest the other suspects involved in the attack.

headline_marked: Trump warns [[China and Russia not to supply weapons to Iran]]
headline: Trump warns China and Russia not to supply weapons to Iran
summary: US President Donald Trump claims Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin have assured him that they will not provide arms to Tehran, despite reports of intelligence sharing.
details: US President Donald Trump warned that it would be "very bad" for China and Russia if they supply weapons to Iran. He stated that he trusts the assurances given by the leaders of both nations to avoid doing so.
The warning comes amid reports that Washington is investigating whether Moscow and Beijing are providing intelligence to Iran following a series of precise attacks on US bases.
Trump shared on Truth Social that during a recent meeting in Beijing, President Xi Jinping assured him that neither the Chinese government nor Chinese companies would sell or supply weapons to Iran.
Similarly, Trump claimed that Russian President Vladimir Putin has given similar assurances, despite the ongoing war in Ukraine, promising that Russia would not sell weapons to Tehran.
US intelligence agencies had previously investigated whether Russia provided targeting information or drone technology to Iran after attacks on CIA targets in the Gulf region.

While the Trump administration has imposed sanctions on several Russian and Chinese entities for helping Iran acquire weapons, some US officials have reported that Russia provides satellite imagery to Iran to monitor US forces.

When questioned about contradictions between his statements and those of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Trump maintained that he believes the assurances of Xi and Putin, stating they have their own interests in keeping these promises.

Trump warns China and Russia: supplying weapons to Iran would be "very bad."

US President Donald Trump warned that it would be "very bad" for China and Russia if they supply weapons to Iran. He stated that he trusts the assurances given by the leaders of both nations to avoid doing so.

The warning comes amid reports that Washington is investigating whether Moscow and Beijing are providing intelligence to Iran following a series of precise attacks on US bases.

Trump shared on Truth Social that during a recent meeting in Beijing, President Xi Jinping assured him that neither the Chinese government nor Chinese companies would sell or supply weapons to Iran.

Similarly, Trump claimed that Russian President Vladimir Putin has given similar assurances, despite the ongoing war in Ukraine, promising that Russia would not sell weapons to Tehran.

US intelligence agencies had previously investigated whether Russia provided targeting information or drone technology to Iran after attacks on CIA targets in the Gulf region.

While the Trump administration has imposed sanctions on several Russian and Chinese entities for helping Iran acquire weapons, some US officials have reported that Russia provides satellite imagery to Iran to monitor US forces.

When questioned about contradictions between his statements and those of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Trump maintained that he believes the assurances of Xi and Putin, stating they have their own interests in keeping these promises.
